subject: Nadia Handoff — RV-2 Launch Campaign Assets Review

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I've got all the draft assets up on the shared drive. The deck, the one-pager, the email sequence, and the landing page copy. I wanted to walk through them with Elena and Jamal before anything goes to production, because you two are the ones who have to use them in front of customers.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Appreciated. Let's start with the one-pager since that's what travels most.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: The one-pager leads with the product name and a single positioning line — 'Precision hardware for demanding environments' — and then breaks into three columns: specifications, integration, and support. I tried to keep it to what a procurement engineer actually wants to know.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: The spec column — is the operating temperature range on there?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It's there. I pulled it from the datasheet Marcus sent me. 0 to 55 degrees Celsius operating.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Good. That comes up constantly with industrial accounts. The Fenstad conversation specifically — they asked about it in our first call.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The positioning line. 'Precision hardware for demanding environments.' I don't hate it, but it could describe any hardware company. Is there something more specific we can say?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I tested three alternatives with two of the beta customer contacts I've been talking to informally. The other options were 'Built for the edge of the network' and 'Where reliability isn't optional.' The current line tested better than both. I know it's general, but it's also the one that didn't confuse people.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I can live with it if the beta contacts responded to it. What's the call to action on the one-pager?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Request a demo or contact sales. The URL goes to a form that routes to Jamal.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: That routing is already set up?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It will be by launch. I need IT — well, Marcus — to confirm the domain redirect is live. I haven't gotten that confirmation yet.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Add that to your list. It needs to be confirmed before we go live.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It's on my list.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The pricing on the one-pager — what number is shown?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: $179 as the introductory price. That's what I had from the pricing discussion when we set the launch plan.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Nadia, the agreed launch price is $189. Where did $179 come from?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: That's what was in the notes I got from the pricing meeting. I have it written down.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I don't know where the disconnect happened but $189 is the number. I've had it in every customer communication I've sent.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: I've been quoting $189 too. I haven't said $179 to anyone.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Okay. If $189 is the agreed number, I'll change it across all the assets. I just want to make sure before I do that we're actually aligned, because if I change it and then it changes again that creates problems downstream.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: $189 is the number. I'm confirming it right now. Update all assets to $189.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Done. I'll have revised assets up by tomorrow morning.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The step-up price — does it appear on the one-pager?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: No. I kept the one-pager to the introductory price only. The step-up is in the email sequence, in the third email, where I explain that the introductory price is available for the first 90 days.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Good. I don't want the step-up price on the one-pager. It creates a conversation I'd rather control in person.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Agreed. Let's look at the email sequence.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: There are five emails. The first goes out on launch day — it's a product announcement, no hard sell. Second email goes three days later and focuses on the integration story — how the RV-2 connects into existing infrastructure. Third email is day seven, that's the one with the introductory pricing and the 90-day window. Fourth is day fourteen, a customer story — I'm using the language from one of the beta contacts, and I've gotten informal approval to use their company name, but I need a written sign-off from them before that email is finalized.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Which customer?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Oskerry Systems. They were enthusiastic about being featured. I just need the sign-off in writing.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: I know their procurement contact. I can get that sign-off faster than going through the marketing channel. Let me handle it.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Please. The fifth email is day twenty-one — a follow-up for non-responders, with a different call to action: a downloadable integration guide rather than a demo request.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: The integration guide — does that exist?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: It's in progress. Marcus is writing the technical section and I'm writing the framing. It should be done by launch.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Should be or will be?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I'm not going to promise something Marcus is half of. I'll say it's on track and flag it if it slips.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Marcus knows it's a launch dependency?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: He knows. He committed to having his section done by May 15th.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Okay. What about the landing page?

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: The landing page has the product image — we're using the render Devon sent, not a photo, since we don't have finished production units to photograph yet — the positioning line, a three-bullet feature summary, the pricing block with the introductory price and the 90-day note, and the demo request form. It's clean. I'll send you the URL for the staging version after this meeting.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Is there a way to see conversion data once the page is live? I want to know which accounts are actually clicking through.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: The form has UTM tracking baked in. You'll see source and campaign in the CRM when a lead comes in. Individual account visibility depends on whether the person fills in their company name.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Most of the people I'm targeting will be coming in from the email sequence, not cold traffic, so they'll probably fill it in.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Nadia, overall I think the assets are in good shape. The price fix is the main thing. Once that's corrected, I'd like to review the final versions before anything goes to print or live.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: Final review with Elena before anything goes live. Got it.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Same for me on the landing page. I want to see it before it's published.

turns.speaker: Nadia
turns.text: I'll send both of you the staging link today and the revised assets tomorrow morning.

decisions: The RV-2 introductory launch price is confirmed as $189; Nadia will update all campaign assets to reflect this.
Revised campaign assets will be ready by the following morning.
Elena and Priya must review and approve final assets before anything goes live or to print.
Jamal will obtain written sign-off from Oskerry Systems for use of their name in the email campaign.

action_items.task: Update all campaign assets (one-pager, email sequence, landing page) to reflect the $189 introductory price and have revised versions on the shared drive by tomorrow morning.
Obtain written sign-off from Oskerry Systems for use of their company name in the RV-2 email campaign.
Confirm with Marcus that the domain redirect for the demo request form is live before launch.
Send Elena and Priya the staging landing page URL today for review.
